title: Compactification independence on the qcqs etale site
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. All derived categories below are the bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For a separated finite-type morphism $h:T\to B$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and a compactification $c=(j:T\hookrightarrow\overline T,p:\overline T\to B)$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper, set $Rh_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. For any two compactifications $c,d$ of $h$ there is a natural isomorphism $Rh_!^c\cong Rh_!^d$, independent of the common refinement used to construct it. These comparisons are identities for equal compactifications and satisfy the cocycle condition for triples.

source.place: Tag 0F7I, label lemma-shriek-well-defined; finite-ring bounded-below specialization

proof.text: Apply [prop-nagata-compactification-category] to $h:T\to B$. Its hypotheses hold since $B$ is qcqs and $h$ is separated of finite type. Write $\operatorname{Comp}(h)$ for its cofiltered category, with no density condition on its objects. An arrow $u:c_1\to c_2$ is a proper $B$-map $u:\overline T_1\to\overline T_2$ with $u j_1=j_2$ and $p_2u=p_1$. Set $F_c=Rp_*j_!$, as in [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. Common refinements and equalizers of parallel arrows below are those asserted by the cofilteredness statement.

Use the natural composition isomorphism $\kappa_{b,a}:R(ba)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rb_*Ra_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] on the small etale ringed topoi with constant coefficient sheaf $\Lambda$. It restricts to the bounded-below categories: direct images there are computed on bounded-below injective representatives by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. These representatives exist by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]; [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives] says that $a_*$ preserves each injective term of $I$; it also preserves zero terms. Thus $a_*I$ is bounded below and termwise injective, and is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. In the normalization of $\kappa$, we can therefore take the resolution $a_*I\to J$ to be the identity. For three composable maps, both composites of $\kappa$ on $QI$ are just the underived identification $(cba)_*I\cong c_*b_*a_*I$. For an identity map they are the identity identification. These underived identifications are coherent on module sheaves: on an etale test object they are restriction along the unique associativity map of the iterated fibre product preserving all projections [def-pc-fibre-product]; both orders give that same map, and it is $\Lambda$-linear by the module formula in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Since every bounded-below object is isomorphic to such a $QI$, naturality proves associativity and the unit laws for $\kappa$ on all objects. Thus we may use coherent identifications $R(ba)_*=Rb_*Ra_*$ in the following formulas.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, label lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; injective computation of composition and its coherence

proof.text: For $u:c_1\to c_2$ use the comparison construction [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], with $X=T$, to obtain $\alpha_u:j_{2!}\to Ru_*j_{1!}$. It is natural in $K$: the restriction, section and derived direct-image identifications defining $\theta_{u,K}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-identification] are functorial. Thus for $f:K\to L$, writing $G=Ru_*j_{1!}$, they give $f\theta_{u,K}=\theta_{u,L}j_2^{-1}G(f)$, or equivalently $j_2^{-1}G(f)\theta_{u,K}^{-1}=\theta_{u,L}^{-1}f$. The natural adjunction bijection in [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison] sends this equality to $G(f)\alpha_{u,K}=\alpha_{u,L}j_{2!}(f)$, which is precisely naturality of $\alpha_u$. Every component is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-iso], hence $\alpha_u$ is a natural isomorphism (the naturality equation for its inverse follows by multiplying the naturality equation on both sides by the inverse components). The hypotheses are exactly a proper $u$, two open immersions with $uj_1=j_2$, finite $\Lambda$ and bounded-below $K$. No cartesian condition on $u^{-1}(j_2(T))$ is required. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-composition], for $v:c_2\to c_3$ we have $\alpha_{vu}=(Rv_*\alpha_u)\alpha_v$ under the composition identification, and the identity comparison is the identity.

source.place: Tags 0F7G (lemma-shriek-lqf-and-proper, separated open case), 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose); used in 0F7I

proof.text: Define $C_u:F_{c_2}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{c_1}$ to be $Rp_{2,*}\alpha_u$ followed by $\kappa_{p_2,u}^{-1}$ at $j_{1!}$; here $p_2u=p_1$. Applying a functor to an isomorphism and composing isomorphisms gives an isomorphism. The preceding two steps imply $C_{vu}=C_uC_v$ and $C_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$. Explicitly, the composite $C_uC_v$ first expands the direct images to $Rp_{3,*}Rv_*Ru_*$, and its comparison factor is $Rp_{3,*}((Rv_*\alpha_u)\alpha_v)=Rp_{3,*}\alpha_{vu}$. Moving the composition isomorphisms past $\alpha_u$ uses their naturality; associativity of $\kappa$ identifies the expansion with $\kappa_{p_3,vu}$. This is precisely $C_{vu}$. The same calculation with identity maps gives the unit law. Thus refinements act contravariantly by coherent isomorphisms of the candidates.

For a common refinement $e\xrightarrow{r}c$, $e\xrightarrow{s}d$ supplied by [prop-nagata-compactification-category], define $I_{c,d}^{e}=C_s^{-1}C_r:F_c\xrightarrow{\sim}F_d$. If $t:e'\to e$ is a further refinement, the comparison through $e'$ is $(C_tC_s)^{-1}(C_tC_r)=C_s^{-1}C_r$ by the composition law and cancellation of $C_t^{-1}C_t$. All these equations are equations of natural transformations, so this produces natural comparisons.

Consider two common refinements $(e,r,s)$ and $(e',r',s')$ of $c,d$. By [prop-nagata-compactification-category], choose $a:z\to e$, $b:z\to e'$. The arrows $ra,r'b:z\to c$ may differ; cofilteredness gives $t:z_1\to z$ equalizing them. Apply the parallel-arrow equalizer clause once more to $sat,s'bt:z_1\to d$, obtaining $t':z_2\to z_1$ that equalizes this pair. The first equality remains true after precomposing with $t'$. On $z_2$ the two pairs of arrows to $c,d$ are therefore equal. Consequently the two ratios of $C$ maps are equal there. By the cancellation calculation in step 5, passing from either $e$ or $e'$ to $z_2$ leaves its ratio unchanged. Hence $I_{c,d}^{e}=I_{c,d}^{e'}$, including independence of the arrows of the common refinement. Denote the common value by $I_{c,d}$. This also explains why density and uniqueness of arrows out of dense objects are unnecessary.

For $c=d$ choose the common refinement $c$ with both arrows the identity. Its ratio is $\mathrm{id}_{F_c}$, so $I_{c,c}=\mathrm{id}$. For three compactifications $c,d,k$, [prop-nagata-compactification-category] gives one common refinement $e$ with arrows $r_c,r_d,r_k$. Independence permits computing all three comparisons through this same $e$. Then $I_{d,k}I_{c,d}=(C_{r_k}^{-1}C_{r_d})(C_{r_d}^{-1}C_{r_c})=C_{r_k}^{-1}C_{r_c}=I_{c,k}$. This is the required cocycle condition, and proves all clauses of the statement.

lean.statement:
theorem rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusIso_eq_refinementIso
    {c d e : Compactification f} (r : e.Refinement c) (s : e.Refinement d) :
    rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusIso Λ c d =
      rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusRefinementIso Λ r ≪≫
        (rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusRefinementIso Λ s).symm
lean.note: Existing declaration family: PlusIso in LowerShriekIndependence constructs the natural isomorphism; LowerShriekCoherence publicly imports it and proves independence for arbitrary common refinements (Iso_eq_refinementIso), identity (Iso_refl), and cocycle (Iso_trans). Parameters are Λ : Type (u + 1), [CommRing Λ], [Finite Λ], {X Y : Scheme.{u}}, {f : X ⟶ Y}, [QuasiCompact f]. This applies to the stated separated finite-type qcqs setting; quasi-compactness of c.i follows from Compactification.quasiCompact_openImmersion. No density or cartesian restriction is imposed on the common refinement. Primary declaration is the arbitrary-refinement independence theorem, defined in the recorded module; the comparison construction is re-exported from LowerShriekIndependence.
